open_questions: A precise photocenter with ground-based multicolour transits would locate the dip; simultaneous aperture photometry in multiple apertures would confirm dilution
dossier.public_summary: The dip looks planet-sized and flat but its depth changes by a factor of three between sectors, and there are large brightness changes outside the dips. Nearby stars only 16 arcsec away can easily make this signal with a stellar eclipse, and the on-target check failed to confirm the source. Together this favours a blended eclipsing binary over a planet on the target star.

reasons.why: Depth more than triples between sectors (108.7% change) even though all are same pipeline. Systematics alone cannot explain this; varying dilution from a neighbour eclipsing binary is the positive match.

reasons.why: Stars inside one TESS pixel can produce the 13610 ppm dip with <25% eclipses, and centroid is inconclusive (HTTPError, no sector with a clear difference image) in both initial checks and centroid_all. No on-target confirmation.
reasons.value: plausible_within_1px 1, could_cause_within_1px 2, could_cause 24; closest that could sep 16.2 arcsec delta_mag 1.17 eclipse_needed 0.0398

reasons.why: Large out-of-transit swing at this period against the dip favours a diluted binary or spot signal over a flat planet transit. Combined with varying depth, it points to blend rather than a planet on the target.
